summary: All five criteria are met. npm test passes 121 of 121 (tests/bash-prose.test.mjs runs 14 of them, all passing when run alone), npm run check passes 11 of 11, and the probes match the tests: file-writing heredoc prose passes, heredocs fed to a shell or interpreter stay scanned, a push followed by prose on the next line passes, and a push whose arguments continue across a backslash-newline or an open construct is denied. Two note-level observations: a file-writing heredoc body is not judged even when its target is a shell startup file, which is the reading C-1 states, and the current guard also allows the same payload written with echo, so this slice adds no new route for that payload; and a push line with a parenthesis joins following prose lines into the push, which over-blocks in the fail-safe direction.

findings.issue: The body of a cat or tee heredoc whose target is a shell startup file is not judged, so a denied command written there as prose passes the guard, as C-1 states.
findings.suggestion: No change required by this slice; a later slice could also judge bodies whose target is a shell startup file or a hook path.

findings.issue: A push line with a parenthesis or other open-construct character joins every following line into the push, so prose on a later line is denied as push arguments; the over-block is in the fail-safe direction.
findings.suggestion: Optional: stop the join at a comment marker on the push line.

evidence.quote: a cat heredoc that only writes a file is prose, not a command line
a heredoc fed to an interpreter is still scanned in full
the push rule and the push deny pattern match within one line
a tee heredoc that names a file is prose, not a command line
a heredoc fed to a shell is still scanned in full
